newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Economist proposed to head Moldova govt.
newsitem.headline: Economist proposed to head Moldova govt.

text.p: Moldovan President Petru Lucinschi on Thursday asked state audit chamber head Ion Chebuk to form a new government and said he should name his cabinet and present a programme to parliament within two weeks.
Lucinschi, elected on December 1 and sworn into office on Wednesday, proposed Chebuk as his candidate for the post of prime minister. Parliament must approve the new premier within two weeks.

Chebuk, a 53-year-old economist, told parliament that he would make reforms to Moldova's shaky financial structures his main priority. Budget arrears have been rising and factories are unable to sell the goods they produce.
Salary and pension arrears, a problem dogging most countries of the former Soviet Union, are more than 200 million lei ($43 million).
"We do not have competitive goods... We are forced to take them to the ex-Soviet market, half as part of the shadow economy, half for barter," Chebuk said.

Chebuk, once Moldova's ambassador to Russia and a former deputy foreign minister, said Moldova's state energy monopoly Moldenergo was bankrupt and the energy sector should be transferred to private hands.
Many Moldovan companies have been privatised since the country launched a programme of market-oriented reforms, but some firms in strategic sectors remain in state hands.
Chebuk said he supported private land ownership, but said Soviet-era collective farms could not be privatised overnight.
"First, we should legally fix peoples' right to own land and to give them the chance of leaving collective farms and form whatever associations they wish," he said.
Lucinschi has already promised to speed up reforms and eliminate crime and poverty in the country of 4.3 million people bordering Ukraine and Romania.
He campaigned on a platform of closer ties with Russia and urged reconciliation with the breakaway Dnestr region, where Slav separatists are seeking their own state.
